newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia bank results fail to give boost to shares.
newsitem.headline: Estonia bank results fail to give boost to shares.

text.p: A batch of results from the top banks failed to give much inspiration to the stock market on Tuesday with trade staying moderate.
The Talse firmed slightly by 0.18 percent to close on 266.31 kroons with 44.2 million kroons of shares traded.
Market capitalisation was a fraction lower at 13.9 billion kroons compared to 14.0 billion kroons.
"Shares did try to rise in the morning, but there were not enough buyers around to support prices and most stocks ended just above yesterday's close or even lower," one dealer said.
"We should expect the same for tomorrow even with some more results due out," he added.
All the leading banks except Uhispank have now issued their April results, seen as generally positive by the market although they had little impact on prices.
"In the long term we could be seeing local investors getting ready for their summer holidays and a quiet time for the next three months," one trader said.
Hoiupank made a big gain in the morning after saying it would increase its 1997 profit forecast after posting a first quarter profit of 17.8 million kroons.
But it ended on trade of 10.5 million kroons with a rise of 1.60 kroons at 130.45.
"By the afternoon there were no buyers about to support the price," a trader said.
Leading bank Hansapank turned over 13.6 million kroons of shares to rise by 0.54 kroons to 138.45 kroons.
Hansapank's April profit was 26.1 million kroons and the 1997 profit to date was 122.5 million kroons.
"There was nothing unexpected in Hansapank's results, the price did move higher to 141 before dropping back to 138.45 kroons," another dealer said.
Over-the-counter market trade saw 9.6 million kroons of shares change hands with diversified industrialist Norma the most active stock.
Norma finished at 75.25 kroons, a decrease of one kroon, after turning over 6.3 million kroons.
